newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lose 1.7 pct in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lose 1.7 pct in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares dropped an average 1.7 percent in weak volume on Thursday amid negative sentiment caused by legal snags to privatisation and March inflation data to be announced on Thursday, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 fell 27 points, or 1.7 percent, to end at 1,565 after moving between 1,554 and 1,602. Trade volume fell sharply to 18.92 trillion lira from Wednesday's 27.38 trillion.
"Negative expectations stemmed from the new challenge to the privatisation law and tomorrow's inflation data,"said Taner Mirza from Es securities.

Turkey's constitutional court began debating this week a request for the annulment of two articles in the privatisation law, concerning the evaluation of state firms slated for privatisation and the sell-off tenders. A ruling is awaited next week.
But the government has already presented to parliament a draft amendment to the privatisation law to redefine the articles expected to be cancelled by the court.
"If March inflation data comes out below expectations and IMF talks produce positive results, the market may recover," Mirza said.
Bankers and analysts predict Turkish consumer price index will rise at around 5.5 to six percent in March, compared to 5.7 percent in February and 5.6 percent in March, 1996.
Some brokers said public offers started on Thursday by Sekerbank and commercial vehicle maker Anadolu-Isuzu which floated part of their share capitals also drained some cash from the market.

Of the 242 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 172 to 28 and 42 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial lost 1.39 percent to 1,561, the IMKB Services dived 2.43 percent to 1,443 and the IMKB Financial shed 1.86 percent to 1,684.
Top actives were utility Cukurova Elektrik, down 7,500 lira at 215,000 and automotive firm Otosan, down 1,000 lira at 78,000. They made up 18.3 percent of the total turnover.
